title: Mini Data Science Framework
description: Built a DataFrame class in Java with linked lists and binary search, plus a generic hash table with collision handling and dynamic resizing. Created Series and DataFrame structures supporting indexing and column operations (UCSD DSC 30).

title: TV Sitcom Data Analysis
description: Analyzed Friends episode, script, and sentiment datasets (7k+ lines, 10 seasons) using Python in Jupyter Notebook. Used bootstrapping and hypothesis testing on directors' IMDb ratings, analyzed gender balance across 6,500+ lines, and built a 2-gram Markov title generator.

title: GroceryDB Visualization
description: Compared Walmart, Target, and Whole Foods on protein, fat, and carbs per dollar across ~19,700 foods. The typical Walmart food gives 2–3× more of each nutrient per dollar than Whole Foods, though differences in product mix and package size mean the gap isn’t a like-for-like price comparison.

title: Predicting Explicit Songs from Spotify Audio Features
description: Can a song's audio features reveal whether it's explicit? Using about 18,000 Spotify tracks across five genres (urban, metal, electronic, acoustic, latin), I explored how audio features like valence differ by genre, tested whether explicit tracks are more energetic, and tested whether tempo is missing at random. A random forest classifier reached a test F1 of about 0.64, up from 0.24 for a two-feature logistic regression baseline. A permutation-test fairness audit showed the model is significantly less precise on metal tracks than on other genres.
